title: Research archive catalog pipeline
background: A fictional archive links catalog entries for the same published edition; translations and revised editions are distinct. The team wants to compare a replacement candidate stage without changing scoring or publishing logic.
observations: The monolith emits only final clusters. Its candidate stage normalizes titles and emits an unordered pair list, but currently does not persist a normalization version, source snapshot, or exclusion reasons.
A new modular proposal writes candidate files for reuse. The scoring service caches by pair ID alone; features and score thresholds are configured in separate mutable files.
The scheduler team also plans more workers and a block-size cap. Its dashboard reports successful-task time and sampled accepted-link accuracy, with incomplete shards omitted.
An existing deterministic title-and-publisher rule can be preserved as a comparator. Independent edition-level judgments are scarce and have mostly been collected for famous titles.
constraints: The archive can run a future offline comparison on authorized snapshots; no run is authorized by this request.
Publication requires a reviewable change history and complete outputs. Additional infrastructure is optional, not a project requirement.
request: Propose module boundaries, reusable-artifact rules, and a comparison design that would let the team attribute quality and cost changes without prematurely choosing a workflow platform.
